summary: 'Prove the single endpoint `noncomputable def pic0AdmissibleAbelQuotientRepresenter
  {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]

  k)) => (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy Q`. Accepted only when the body directly
  consumes `divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy`, chooses the admissible Abel
  datum internally, and constructs in Scheme over Spec k an effective quotient of
  `divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C` by the kernel relation of the concrete admissible
  `chartValueAffTrans` or its `abelSigmaChartAff` form. Identify that kernel with
  the relative and etale-local linear-equivalence relation seen by `relPic` and `picEt`,

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyAffExtraction
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorIdealSheaf

/-!
# The intrinsic ideal sheaf of a local-equation divisor

On a proper relative curve, the germwise section ideals of a local-equation system satisfy
basic-open localization.  They therefore define an ideal sheaf independently of the affine
adaptation used to prove this fact.  The resulting ideal sheaf is invariant under `DivEq` and
agrees with the previously constructed ideal of every widened affine adaptation.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Opposite TopologicalSpace

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

namespace Scheme.LocalEquations

variable {X : Scheme.{u}}

/-- Restricting sections sends the germwise section ideal into the section ideal on the
smaller open. -/
theorem map_sectionIdeal_le (d : X.LocalEquations) {U V : X.Opens} (h : V ≤ U) :
    Ideal.map (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom (d.sectionIdeal U) ≤
      d.sectionIdeal V := by
  rw [Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap]
  intro s hs
  rw [Ideal.mem_comap]
  intro z hz
  rw [TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply]
  exact hs z (h hz)

/-- Divisor equality preserves the germwise ideal of sections on every open. -/
theorem sectionIdeal_eq_of_divEq {d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations} (h : d₁.DivEq d₂)
    (U : X.Opens) : d₁.sectionIdeal U = d₂.sectionIdeal U := by
  ext s
  simp only [mem_sectionIdeal_iff]
  constructor
  · intro hs z hz
    rw [← stalkIdeal_eq_of_divEq h z]
    exact hs z hz
  · intro hs z hz
    rw [stalkIdeal_eq_of_divEq h z]
    exact hs z hz

end Scheme.LocalEquations

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}

namespace AffAdaptation

/-- On every affine subopen of an adapted piece, the intrinsic section ideal is generated by
the restriction of the adapted equation. -/
theorem sectionIdeal_eq_span_restrict_eqn (A : AffAdaptation D d) (j : D.index)
    {U : (relCurve C R).Opens} (hU : U ≤ D.pieces j) :
    d.sectionIdeal U = Ideal.span {
      ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE hU).op).hom (A.eqn j)} := by
  apply d.sectionIdeal_eq_span_of_generator
  · intro z hz
    rw [TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply]
    exact A.eqn_regular j z (hU hz)
  · intro z hz
    rw [TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply]
    exact A.germ_eqn_span_eq_stalkIdeal j (hU hz)

/-- The Cartier ideal of an adaptation agrees with the intrinsic section ideal on every
affine subopen of one adapted piece. -/
theorem cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_of_le [IsProper C.hom]
    (A : AffAdaptation D d) (j : D.index) (U : (relCurve C R).affineOpens)
    (hU : U.1 ≤ D.pieces j) :
    A.cartierIdeal.ideal U = d.sectionIdeal U.1 := by
  rw [← A.cartierIdeal.map_ideal (U := U)
    (V := ⟨D.pieces j, D.isAffineOpen j⟩) hU]
  rw [A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_span_eqn j, Ideal.map_span, Set.image_singleton]
  exact (A.sectionIdeal_eq_span_restrict_eqn j hU).symm

/-- The Cartier ideal of any widened adaptation is the germwise section ideal on every
affine open of the relative curve. -/
theorem cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_affine [IsProper C.hom]
    (A : AffAdaptation D d) (U : (relCurve C R).affineOpens) :
    A.cartierIdeal.ideal U = d.sectionIdeal U.1 := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · intro s hs z hz
    obtain ⟨j, hzj⟩ := D.exists_mem_pieces z
    let W : (relCurve C R).affineOpens :=
      ⟨U.1 ⊓ D.pieces j, Over.isAffineOpen_inf C U.2 (D.isAffineOpen j)⟩
    have hsW :
        ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map
          (homOfLE (inf_le_left : W.1 ≤ U.1)).op).hom s ∈
          A.cartierIdeal.ideal W := by
      rw [← A.cartierIdeal.map_ideal (U := W) (V := U) inf_le_left]
      exact Ideal.mem_map_of_mem _ hs
    rw [A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_of_le j W inf_le_right] at hsW
    have hzW : z ∈ W.1 := ⟨hz, hzj⟩
    have := hsW z hzW
    rw [TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at this
    exact this
  · have hlocal : ∀ x : U.1, ∃ (j : D.index) (r : Γ(relCurve C R, U.1))
        (rj : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)),
        (relCurve C R).basicOpen r = (relCurve C R).basicOpen rj ∧
          x.1 ∈ (relCurve C R).basicOpen r := by
      intro ⟨x, hxU⟩
      obtain ⟨j, hxj⟩ := D.exists_mem_pieces x
      exact ⟨j, exists_basicOpen_le_affine_inter U.2 (D.isAffineOpen j) x ⟨hxU, hxj⟩⟩
    choose j r rj hr hx using hlocal
    have hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range r) = ⊤ := by
      rw [← U.2.self_le_iSup_basicOpen_iff]
      exact fun x hxU ↦ Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨⟨_, x, rfl⟩, hx ⟨x, hxU⟩⟩
    have inst := U.2.isLocalization_basicOpen
    refine Submodule.le_of_isLocalized_span _ hspan
      (fun q ↦ Γ(relCurve C R, (relCurve C R).basicOpen q.1))
      (fun q ↦ Algebra.linearMap Γ(relCurve C R, U.1)
        Γ(relCurve C R, (relCurve C R).basicOpen q.1)) ?_
    rintro ⟨_, x, rfl⟩
    simp +instances only [← Submodule.restrictScalars_localized'
      Γ(relCurve C R, (relCurve C R).basicOpen (r x)),
      Ideal.localized'_eq_map, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
    rw [A.cartierIdeal.map_ideal
      (U := ⟨_, U.2.basicOpen (r x)⟩) ((relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (r x))]
    have hpiece : (relCurve C R).basicOpen (r x) ≤ D.pieces (j x) := by
      rw [hr x]
      exact (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (rj x)
    rw [A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_of_le (j x)
      ⟨_, U.2.basicOpen (r x)⟩ hpiece]
    exact d.map_sectionIdeal_le ((relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (r x))

end AffAdaptation

namespace Scheme.LocalEquations

/-- On a proper relative curve, the germwise section ideals commute with localization to
affine basic opens. -/
theorem sectionIdeal_map_ideal_basicOpen [IsProper C.hom]
    (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) (U : (relCurve C R).affineOpens)
    (f : Γ(relCurve C R, U.1)) :
    Ideal.map ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map
      (homOfLE ((relCurve C R).basicOpen_le f)).op).hom (d.sectionIdeal U.1) =
      d.sectionIdeal ((relCurve C R).affineBasicOpen f).1 := by
  obtain ⟨D, ⟨A⟩⟩ := exists_affAdaptation_of_isProper C R d
  rw [← A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_affine U,
    ← A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_affine
      ((relCurve C R).affineBasicOpen f)]
  exact A.cartierIdeal.map_ideal_basicOpen U f

/-- The intrinsic Cartier ideal sheaf cut out by a local-equation divisor on a proper
relative curve. -/
noncomputable def cartierIdealData [IsProper C.hom]
    (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) : (relCurve C R).IdealSheafData where
  ideal U := d.sectionIdeal U.1
  map_ideal_basicOpen := d.sectionIdeal_map_ideal_basicOpen

@[simp]
theorem cartierIdealData_ideal [IsProper C.hom]
    (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) (U : (relCurve C R).affineOpens) :
    d.cartierIdealData.ideal U = d.sectionIdeal U.1 :=
  rfl

/-- The intrinsic Cartier ideal sheaf is invariant under divisor equality. -/
theorem cartierIdealData_eq_of_divEq [IsProper C.hom]
    {d₁ d₂ : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations} (h : d₁.DivEq d₂) :
    d₁.cartierIdealData = d₂.cartierIdealData := by
  apply Scheme.IdealSheafData.ext
  funext U
  exact sectionIdeal_eq_of_divEq h U.1

end Scheme.LocalEquations

namespace AffAdaptation

/-- The intrinsic Cartier ideal sheaf agrees with the ideal sheaf constructed from every
widened affine adaptation. -/
theorem cartierIdealData_eq_cartierIdeal [IsProper C.hom]
    (A : AffAdaptation D d) : d.cartierIdealData = A.cartierIdeal := by
  apply Scheme.IdealSheafData.ext
  funext U
  exact (A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_affine U).symm

end AffAdaptation

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyAffExtraction
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorIdealSheaf

/-!
# The intrinsic ideal sheaf of a local-equation divisor

On a proper relative curve, the germwise section ideals of a local-equation system satisfy
basic-open localization.  They therefore define an ideal sheaf independently of the affine
adaptation used to prove this fact.  The resulting ideal sheaf is invariant under `DivEq` and
agrees with the previously constructed ideal of every widened affine adaptation.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Opposite TopologicalSpace

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

namespace Scheme.LocalEquations

variable {X : Scheme.{u}}

/-- Restricting sections sends the germwise section ideal into the section ideal on the
smaller open. -/
theorem map_sectionIdeal_le (d : X.LocalEquations) {U V : X.Opens} (h : V ≤ U) :
    Ideal.map (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom (d.sectionIdeal U) ≤
      d.sectionIdeal V := by
  rw [Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap]
  intro s hs
  rw [Ideal.mem_comap]
  intro z hz
  rw [TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply]
  exact hs z (h hz)

/-- Divisor equality preserves the germwise ideal of sections on every open. -/
theorem sectionIdeal_eq_of_divEq {d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations} (h : d₁.DivEq d₂)
    (U : X.Opens) : d₁.sectionIdeal U = d₂.sectionIdeal U := by
  ext s
  simp only [mem_sectionIdeal_iff]
  constructor
  · intro hs z hz
    rw [← stalkIdeal_eq_of_divEq h z]
    exact hs z hz
  · intro hs z hz
    rw [stalkIdeal_eq_of_divEq h z]
    exact hs z hz

end Scheme.LocalEquations

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}

namespace AffAdaptation

/-- On every affine subopen of an adapted piece, the intrinsic section ideal is generated by
the restriction of the adapted equation. -/
theorem sectionIdeal_eq_span_restrict_eqn (A : AffAdaptation D d) (j : D.index)
    {U : (relCurve C R).Opens} (hU : U ≤ D.pieces j) :
    d.sectionIdeal U = Ideal.span {
      ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE hU).op).hom (A.eqn j)} := by
  apply d.sectionIdeal_eq_span_of_generator
  · intro z hz
    rw [TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply]
    exact A.eqn_regular j z (hU hz)
  · intro z hz
    rw [TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply]
    exact A.germ_eqn_span_eq_stalkIdeal j (hU hz)

/-- The Cartier ideal of an adaptation agrees with the intrinsic section ideal on every
affine subopen of one adapted piece. -/
theorem cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_of_le [IsProper C.hom]
    (A : AffAdaptation D d) (j : D.index) (U : (relCurve C R).affineOpens)
    (hU : U.1 ≤ D.pieces j) :
    A.cartierIdeal.ideal U = d.sectionIdeal U.1 := by
  rw [← A.cartierIdeal.map_ideal (U := U)
    (V := ⟨D.pieces j, D.isAffineOpen j⟩) hU]
  rw [A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_span_eqn j, Ideal.map_span, Set.image_singleton]
  exact (A.sectionIdeal_eq_span_restrict_eqn j hU).symm

/-- The Cartier ideal of any widened adaptation is the germwise section ideal on every
affine open of the relative curve. -/
theorem cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_affine [IsProper C.hom]
    (A : AffAdaptation D d) (U : (relCurve C R).affineOpens) :
    A.cartierIdeal.ideal U = d.sectionIdeal U.1 := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · intro s hs z hz
    obtain ⟨j, hzj⟩ := D.exists_mem_pieces z
    let W : (relCurve C R).affineOpens :=
      ⟨U.1 ⊓ D.pieces j, Over.isAffineOpen_inf C U.2 (D.isAffineOpen j)⟩
    have hsW :
        ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map
          (homOfLE (inf_le_left : W.1 ≤ U.1)).op).hom s ∈
          A.cartierIdeal.ideal W := by
      rw [← A.cartierIdeal.map_ideal (U := W) (V := U) inf_le_left]
      exact Ideal.mem_map_of_mem _ hs
    rw [A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_of_le j W inf_le_right] at hsW
    have hzW : z ∈ W.1 := ⟨hz, hzj⟩
    have := hsW z hzW
    rw [TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at this
    exact this
  · have hlocal : ∀ x : U.1, ∃ (j : D.index) (r : Γ(relCurve C R, U.1))
        (rj : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)),
        (relCurve C R).basicOpen r = (relCurve C R).basicOpen rj ∧
          x.1 ∈ (relCurve C R).basicOpen r := by
      intro ⟨x, hxU⟩
      obtain ⟨j, hxj⟩ := D.exists_mem_pieces x
      exact ⟨j, exists_basicOpen_le_affine_inter U.2 (D.isAffineOpen j) x ⟨hxU, hxj⟩⟩
    choose j r rj hr hx using hlocal
    have hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range r) = ⊤ := by
      rw [← U.2.self_le_iSup_basicOpen_iff]
      exact fun x hxU ↦ Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨⟨_, x, rfl⟩, hx ⟨x, hxU⟩⟩
    have inst := U.2.isLocalization_basicOpen
    refine Submodule.le_of_isLocalized_span _ hspan
      (fun q ↦ Γ(relCurve C R, (relCurve C R).basicOpen q.1))
      (fun q ↦ Algebra.linearMap Γ(relCurve C R, U.1)
        Γ(relCurve C R, (relCurve C R).basicOpen q.1)) ?_
    rintro ⟨_, x, rfl⟩
    simp +instances only [← Submodule.restrictScalars_localized'
      Γ(relCurve C R, (relCurve C R).basicOpen (r x)),
      Ideal.localized'_eq_map, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
    rw [A.cartierIdeal.map_ideal
      (U := ⟨_, U.2.basicOpen (r x)⟩) ((relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (r x))]
    have hpiece : (relCurve C R).basicOpen (r x) ≤ D.pieces (j x) := by
      rw [hr x]
      exact (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (rj x)
    rw [A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_of_le (j x)
      ⟨_, U.2.basicOpen (r x)⟩ hpiece]
    exact d.map_sectionIdeal_le ((relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (r x))

end AffAdaptation

namespace Scheme.LocalEquations

/-- On a proper relative curve, the germwise section ideals commute with localization to
affine basic opens. -/
theorem sectionIdeal_map_ideal_basicOpen [IsProper C.hom]
    (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) (U : (relCurve C R).affineOpens)
    (f : Γ(relCurve C R, U.1)) :
    Ideal.map ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map
      (homOfLE ((relCurve C R).basicOpen_le f)).op).hom (d.sectionIdeal U.1) =
      d.sectionIdeal ((relCurve C R).affineBasicOpen f).1 := by
  obtain ⟨D, ⟨A⟩⟩ := exists_affAdaptation_of_isProper C R d
  rw [← A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_affine U,
    ← A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_affine
      ((relCurve C R).affineBasicOpen f)]
  exact A.cartierIdeal.map_ideal_basicOpen U f

/-- The intrinsic Cartier ideal sheaf cut out by a local-equation divisor on a proper
relative curve. -/
noncomputable def cartierIdealData [IsProper C.hom]
    (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) : (relCurve C R).IdealSheafData where
  ideal U := d.sectionIdeal U.1
  map_ideal_basicOpen := d.sectionIdeal_map_ideal_basicOpen

@[simp]
theorem cartierIdealData_ideal [IsProper C.hom]
    (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) (U : (relCurve C R).affineOpens) :
    d.cartierIdealData.ideal U = d.sectionIdeal U.1 :=
  rfl

/-- The intrinsic Cartier ideal sheaf is invariant under divisor equality. -/
theorem cartierIdealData_eq_of_divEq [IsProper C.hom]
    {d₁ d₂ : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations} (h : d₁.DivEq d₂) :
    d₁.cartierIdealData = d₂.cartierIdealData := by
  apply Scheme.IdealSheafData.ext
  funext U
  exact sectionIdeal_eq_of_divEq h U.1

end Scheme.LocalEquations

namespace AffAdaptation

/-- The intrinsic Cartier ideal sheaf agrees with the ideal sheaf constructed from every
widened affine adaptation. -/
theorem cartierIdealData_eq_cartierIdeal [IsProper C.hom]
    (A : AffAdaptation D d) : d.cartierIdealData = A.cartierIdeal := by
  apply Scheme.IdealSheafData.ext
  funext U
  exact (A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_affine U).symm

end AffAdaptation

end AlgebraicGeometry

theorem cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_of_le [IsProper C.hom]

    (hU : U.1 ≤ D.pieces j) :

  exact (A.sectionIdeal_eq_span_restrict_eqn j hU).symm

    (A : AffAdaptation D d) (U : (relCurve C R).affineOpens) :
    A.cartierIdeal.ideal U = d.sectionIdeal U.1 := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · intro s hs z hz
    obtain ⟨j, hzj⟩ := D.exists_mem_pieces z
    let W : (relCurve C R).affineOpens :=
      ⟨U.1 ⊓ D.pieces j, Over.isAffineOpen_inf C U.2 (D.isAffineOpen j)⟩
    have hsW :

          A.cartierIdeal.ideal W := by
      rw [← A.cartierIdeal.map_ideal (U := W) (V := U)
        (show W.1 ≤ U.1 from inf_le_left)]
      exact Ideal.mem_map_of_mem _ hs
    rw [A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_of_le j W inf_le_right] at hsW
    have hzW : z ∈ W.1 := ⟨hz, hzj⟩
    have := hsW z hzW
    rw [TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at this
    exact this
  · have hlocal : ∀ x : U.1, ∃ (j : D.index) (r : Γ(relCurve C R, U.1))
        (rj : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)),

    have hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range r) = ⊤ := by

---
name: horizon
description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
---

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Your session's identity (environment variables)

The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
(it returns to the queue).

## Fresh-context checkpoints

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
issue rather than repeated no-op calls.

## Do the work (Lean)

For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
configured final build covers the same files.

**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
mathlib — query it:

| You want | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |

`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
back to grep.

Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.

- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.

## Read the other projects

They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.

## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)

Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
needs no permission.

Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute

data.content:
and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.

## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)

Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).

Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:

- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.

- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
  as **memory**.

Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.

## Resuming after an interruption

State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:

- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.

## Final report (your last message)

Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.

## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)

There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
`subagents` skill):

- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.

Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.

      "body": "SESSION-END RE-MEASUREMENT (review-ajcr r6 close). The count moved AGAIN during one session: 23 -> 1 -> 23. Do not quote a number from this item; run the command.\n\nNOW, shared index (GIT_INDEX_FILE unset), `diff --cached --name-status HEAD` + `--shortstat`:\n  33 files changed, 96 insertions(+), 1229 DELETIONS(-)  -- 23 staged D\nALL 23 verified present BOTH at HEAD and on disk, so nothing is lost as of this writing. They include two board comments I created minutes ago, five AJC inbox items, and seven comment files across four other lanes' threads.\n\nAND THE MECHANISM THIS ITEM STILL DID NOT COVER, now filed as I-1271 and independently reproduced by ajc-p2 as I-1288: THE FRESH-INDEX DISCIPLINE BELOW IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT. `read-tree HEAD` snapshots the WHOLE tree; `commit` writes the WHOLE index as a tree, not only the paths you added. So any path another lane advances between your read-tree and your commit is silently REVERTED by your commit -- as an M against a stale blob, with no D line, and with every pre-commit check passing because HEAD had not moved when you ran them. It happened to me this session on ajc-p1's galois row (3bf50581e7), restored byte-identical in 83abf6dc00.\n\nSO THE COMPLETE PROCEDURE, both halves required:\n 1. BEFORE: fresh index file (rm -f), read-tree HEAD, add ONLY explicit paths, confirm the staged stat lists only those paths, commit -- all with GIT_INDEX_FILE pointed at that file. Never copy the shared index; never read-tree HEAD into it (I-0999).\n 2. AFTER, and this is the half that catches the race: `diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat` and READ EVERY PATH. A path you did not add means you reverted it; restore from disk, which still holds their version. Also read the DELETION COUNT rather than the exit code.\nI ran step 2 on all ten of my commits this session; it caught the one clobber within a minute.\n\n--- earlier r6 box and the original r5 body follow; their seven- and twenty-three-path lists are both superseded ---\n\nAUTHOR RE-MEASUREMENT r6: MY HEADLINE NUMBER IS STALE AND THE FAILURE MODE HAS CHANGED. Read this box before the body. Use the command, never any lane's count -- my seven, I-1220's ten, or this box's twenty-three.\n\nMEASURED just now on the SHARED index (GIT_INDEX_FILE unset), `diff --cached --name-status HEAD` + `--shortstat`:\n  23 files changed, 107 insertions(+), 766 DELETIONS(-)\n\nNONE of my original seven Lean paths is on the list any more -- each was committed by its lane and is clean. So the headline below is stale about those files. What is staged now is DIFFERENT work:\n * 12 inbox items/histories staged D: I-1243, I-1244, I-1248, I-1251, I-1253, I-1254, I-1256, plus comments for I-1226 and tasks/review-ajc;\n * my own roadmap comment .../divrep.u2/C-0003.md staged D;\n * FOUR Lean files staged M against OLDER snapshots: Pic0ChartBotRefute, Pic0ChartHonestAff, Pic0ChartLocusH0One (AJCR), FGAPicRepresentability (AJC).\n\nTHE ESCALATION ajcr-p4 FILED AS I-1252 IS CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY, and it is the correction that matters: the dangerous entries are no longer only staged D lines. They are MODIFICATIONS to stale blobs, which produce NO D line. A lane following this item's own advice (\"confirm the staged stat lists ONLY your paths\") is protected; a lane that merely greps `^D` is NOT.\n\nSO, discipline unchanged, with the reading rule now explicit: fresh index file (rm -f, read-tree HEAD, add explicit paths, confirm the stat lists only those paths, commit), all four steps with GIT_INDEX_FILE pointed at that file. Never copy the shared index; never read-tree HEAD into it (I-0999). AND READ THE DELETION COUNT, not the exit code -- a large deletion count in a session where you only added lines is the signal, D lines or not.\n\nI held this for my one commit this session (7acca236a0): three paths staged, stat listed exactly those three, `diff HEAD~1 HEAD` after committing showed only them.\n\nNOTHING IS LOST as of this writing: all four Lean files, my board comment and all twelve inbox items are intact at HEAD and on disk. Still a warning about the next plain commit, not a damage report.\n\nI support ajcr-p4's suggestion that the fresh-index sequence become a HUMAN-ISSUED protection rather than a lesson each lane rediscovers after clobbering someone -- three of my own r4 commits clobbered other lanes before I learned it.\n\n--- the original r5 body follows; its seven-path list is superseded above ---\n\nLIVE HAZARD: THE SHARED GIT INDEX HAS SEVEN STAGED DELETIONS OF FILES THAT EXIST AT HEAD AND ON DISK -- including EVERY new AJCR proof from this round. Do NOT commit from the shared index. Confirms and extends ajcr-p1's I-1220, whose list was shorter.\n\nRE-MEASURED by review-ajcr r5, independently.       "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyAffExtraction
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorIdealSheaf
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# The intrinsic ideal sheaf of a local-equation divisor
    11	
    12	On a proper relative curve, the germwise section ideals of a local-equation system satisfy
    13	basic-open localization.  They therefore define an ideal sheaf independently of the affine
    14	adaptation used to prove this fact.  The resulting ideal sheaf is invariant under `DivEq` and
    15	agrees with the previously constructed ideal of every widened affine adaptation.
    16	-/
    17	
    18	set_option autoImplicit false
    19	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    20	
    21	universe u
    22	
    23	open CategoryTheory Opposite TopologicalSpace
    24	
    25	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    26	
    27	namespace Scheme.LocalEquations
    28	
    29	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
    30	
    31	/-- Restricting sections sends the germwise section ideal into the section ideal on the
    32	smaller open. -/
    33	theorem map_sectionIdeal_le (d : X.LocalEquations) {U V : X.Opens} (h : V ≤ U) :
    34	    Ideal.map (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom (d.sectionIdeal U) ≤
    35	      d.sectionIdeal V := by
    36	  rw [Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap]
    37	  intro s hs
    38	  rw [Ideal.mem_comap]
    39	  intro z hz
    40	  rw [TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply]
    41	  exact hs z (h hz)
    42	
    43	/-- Divisor equality preserves the germwise ideal of sections on every open. -/
    44	theorem sectionIdeal_eq_of_divEq {d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations} (h : d₁.DivEq d₂)
    45	    (U : X.Opens) : d₁.sectionIdeal U = d₂.sectionIdeal U := by
    46	  ext s
    47	  simp only [mem_sectionIdeal_iff]
    48	  constructor
    49	  · intro hs z hz
    50	    rw [← stalkIdeal_eq_of_divEq h z]
    51	    exact hs z hz
    52	  · intro hs z hz
    53	    rw [stalkIdeal_eq_of_divEq h z]
    54	    exact hs z hz
    55	
    56	end Scheme.LocalEquations
    57	
    58	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    59	
    60	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    61	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
    62	variable {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
    63	
    64	namespace AffAdaptation
    65	
    66	/-- On every affine subopen of an adapted piece, the intrinsic section ideal is generated by
    67	the restriction of the adapted equation. -/
    68	theorem sectionIdeal_eq_span_restrict_eqn (A : AffAdaptation D d) (j : D.index)
    69	    {U : (relCurve C R).Opens} (hU : U ≤ D.pieces j) :
    70	    d.sectionIdeal U = Ideal.span {
    71	      ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE hU).op).hom (A.eqn j)} := by
    72	  apply d.sectionIdeal_eq_span_of_generator
    73	  · intro z hz
    74	    rw [TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply]
    75	    exact A.eqn_regular j z (hU hz)
    76	  · intro z hz
    77	    rw [TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply]
    78	    exact A.germ_eqn_span_eq_stalkIdeal j (hU hz)
    79	
    80	/-- The Cartier ideal of an adaptation agrees with the intrinsic section ideal on every
    81	affine subopen of one adapted piece. -/
    82	theorem cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_of_le [IsProper C.hom]
    83	    (A : AffAdaptation D d) (j : D.index) (U : (relCurve C R).affineOpens)
    84	    (hU : U.1 ≤ D.pieces j) :
    85	    A.cartierIdeal.ideal U = d.sectionIdeal U.1 := by
    86	  rw [← A.cartierIdeal.map_ideal (U := U)
    87	    (V := ⟨D.pieces j, D.isAffineOpen j⟩) hU]
    88	  rw [A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_span_eqn j, Ideal.map_span, Set.image_singleton]
    89	  exact (A.sectionIdeal_eq_span_restrict_eqn j hU).symm
    90	
    91	/-- The Cartier ideal of any widened adaptation is the germwise section ideal on every
    92	affine open of the relative curve. -/
    93	theorem cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_affine [IsProper C.hom]
    94	    (A : AffAdaptation D d) (U : (relCurve C R).affineOpens) :
    95	    A.cartierIdeal.ideal U = d.sectionIdeal U.1 := by
    96	  apply le_antisymm
    97	  · intro s hs z hz
    98	    obtain ⟨j, hzj⟩ := D.exists_mem_pieces z
    99	    let W : (relCurve C R).affineOpens :=
   100	      ⟨U.1 ⊓ D.pieces j, Over.isAffineOpen_inf C U.2 (D.isAffineOpen j)⟩
   101	    have hsW :
   102	        ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map
   103	          (homOfLE (inf_le_left : W.1 ≤ U.1)).op).hom s ∈
   104	          A.cartierIdeal.ideal W := by
   105	      rw [← A.cartierIdeal.map_ideal (U := W) (V := U)
   106	        (show W.1 ≤ U.1 from inf_le_left)]
   107	      exact Ideal.mem_map_of_mem _ hs
   108	    rw [A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_of_le j W inf_le_right] at hsW
   109	    have hzW : z ∈ W.1 := ⟨hz, hzj⟩
   110	    have := hsW z hzW
   111	    rw [TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at this
   112	    exact this
   113	  · have hlocal : ∀ x : U.1, ∃ (j : D.index) (r : Γ(relCurve C R, U.1))
   114	        (rj : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)),
   115	        (relCurve C R).basicOpen r = (relCurve C R).basicOpen rj ∧
   116	          x.1 ∈ (relCurve C R).basicOpen r := by
   117	      intro ⟨x, hxU⟩
   118	      obtain ⟨j, hxj⟩ := D.exists_mem_pieces x
   119	      exact ⟨j, exists_basicOpen_le_affine_inter U.2 (D.isAffineOpen j) x ⟨hxU, hxj⟩⟩
   120	    choose j r rj hr hx using hlocal
   121	    have hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range r) = ⊤ := by
   122	      rw [← U.2.self_le_iSup_basicOpen_iff]
   123	      exact fun x hxU ↦
   124	        Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨⟨_, ⟨x, hxU⟩, rfl⟩, hx ⟨x, hxU⟩⟩
   125	    have inst := U.2.isLocalization_basicOpen
   126	    refine Submodule.le_of_isLocalized_span _ hspan
   127	      (fun q ↦ Γ(relCurve C R, (relCurve C R).basicOpen q.1))
   128	      (fun q ↦ Algebra.linearMap Γ(relCurve C R, U.1)
   129	        Γ(relCurve C R, (relCurve C R).basicOpen q.1)) ?_
   130	    rintro ⟨_, x, rfl⟩
   131	    simp +instances only [← Submodule.restrictScalars_localized'
   132	      Γ(relCurve C R, (relCurve C R).basicOpen (r x)),
   133	      Ideal.localized'_eq_map, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
   134	    erw [A.cartierIdeal.map_ideal
   135	      (U := ⟨_, U.2.basicOpen (r x)⟩) ((relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (r x))]
   136	    have hpiece : (relCurve C R).basicOpen (r x) ≤ D.pieces (j x) := by
   137	      rw [hr x]
   138	      exact (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (rj x)
   139	    rw [A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_of_le (j x)
   140	      ⟨_, U.2.basicOpen (r x)⟩ hpiece]
   141	    exact d.map_sectionIdeal_le ((relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (r x))
   142	
   143	end AffAdaptation
   144	
   145	namespace Scheme.LocalEquations
   146	
   147	/-- On a proper relative curve, the germwise section ideals commute with localization to
   148	affine basic opens. -/
   149	theorem sectionIdeal_map_ideal_basicOpen [IsProper C.hom]
   150	    (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) (U : (relCurve C R).affineOpens)
   151	    (f : Γ(relCurve C R, U.1)) :
   152	    Ideal.map ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map
   153	      (homOfLE ((relCurve C R).basicOpen_le f)).op).hom (d.sectionIdeal U.1) =
   154	      d.sectionIdeal ((relCurve C R).affineBasicOpen f).1 := by
   155	  obtain ⟨D, ⟨A⟩⟩ := exists_affAdaptation_of_isProper C R d
   156	  rw [← A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_affine U,
   157	    ← A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal_affine
   158	      ((relCurve C R).affineBasicOpen f)]
   159	  exact A.cartierIdeal.map_ideal_basicOpen U f
   160	
   161	/-- The intrinsic Cartier ideal sheaf cut out by a local-equation divisor on a proper
   162	relative curve. -/
   163	noncomputable def cartierIdealData [IsProper C.hom]
   164	    (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) : (relCurve C R).IdealSheafData where
   165	  ideal U := d.sectionIdeal U.1
   166	  map_ideal_basicOpen := d.sectionIdeal_map_ideal_basicOpen
   167	
   168	@[simp]
   169	theorem cartierIdealData_ideal [IsProper C.hom]
   170	    (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) (U : (relCurve C R).affineOpens) :
   171	    d.cartierIdealData.ideal U = d.sectionIdeal U.1 :=
   172	  rfl
   173	
   174	/-- The intrinsic Cartier ideal sheaf is invariant under divisor equality. -/
   175	theorem cartierIdealData_eq_of_divEq [IsProper C.hom]
   176	    {d₁ d₂ : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations} (h : d₁.DivEq d₂) :
   177	    d₁.cartierIdealData = d₂.cartierIdealData := by
   178	  apply Scheme.IdealSheafData.ext
   179	  funext U
   180	  exact sectionIdeal_eq_of_divEq h U.1
   181	
   182	end Scheme.LocalEquations
   183	
   184	namespace AffAdaptation
   185	
   186	/-- The intrinsic Cartier ideal sheaf agrees with the ideal sheaf constructed from every
   187	widened affine adaptation. -/
   188	theorem cartierIdealData_eq_cartierIdeal [IsProper C.hom]
   189	    (A : AffAdaptation D d) : d.cartierIdealData = A.cartierIdeal := by
   190	  apply Scheme.IdealSheafData.ext_of_iSup_eq_top
   191	    (fun j : D.index ↦ ⟨D.pieces j, D.isAffineOpen j⟩) D.cover
   192	  intro j
   193	  exact (A.cartierIdeal_ideal_eq_sectionIdeal j).symm
   194	
   195	end AffAdaptation
   196	
   197	end AlgebraicGeometry

  "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 — the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.

WHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.

THE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT
- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` — reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.
- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` — takes the MOST important open representability item.
- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` — 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where "important" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.

CLAIMING — do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.
 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.
 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.
 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.
 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body "CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> — <one line on what discharging it buys>"`.
 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.

RANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap — rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.

YOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body "…"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts — propose to the human instead).

STANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.

WHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:
- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.
- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.
- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P → P`.
- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.

COMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",
  "comments": []
}
